# evestack

> An open source workspace for recurring AI work on infrastructure you control. Start a task,
> inspect its result and evidence, answer configured tool decisions, and schedule tested work.
> Eve Stack packages the eve runtime with a dashboard, Postgres history and operator tools.

The initial use case is a repository maintenance brief: connect one repository, report recent
changes and issues with source links, inspect the result, then test and enable a routine.
See `/docs/first-task`. A completed task is not proof of a correct answer or external effect.

Apache-2.0 software without a software subscription fee. Hardware, hosting, electricity, model
usage and connected services may cost money. Cloud providers receive prompts; optional Composio
is hosted and holds connected-account tokens. External tools receive the data needed for calls.
Never describe the stack as costing nothing or as universally local, private or safe.

eve is a trademark of Vercel. Eve Stack is independent and unaffiliated. It is a distribution,
not a fork, and does not claim to be the first self-hosted eve project.

## For coding agents

`https://evestack.vercel.app/agent.md` serves the setup pack from `skills/evestack`, including its
reference files. `npx evestack skills` installs the pack bundled with its CLI release; the
website pack follows the deployed website and may differ. The full documentation
corpus is `https://evestack.vercel.app/llms-full.txt`; this file is the index.

`@evestack/mcp` uses the dashboard HTTP APIs for task history, routines, decisions, readiness,
recovery, memory reviews and regression cases. Task mutations require
`EVESTACK_MCP_ALLOW_CONTROL=1`; decisions also require `EVESTACK_MCP_ALLOW_APPROVALS=1`.
Read-only access does not imply control or approval authority.

## Version and operating facts

- `release-manifest.json` records selected package/runtime/storage versions for the source
  checkout. Check installed and deployed versions separately. Changelog headings and source
  manifests do not prove publication. Components are independently versioned.
- This candidate selects Eve `^0.54.3` and exact `@workflow/world-postgres` `5.0.0-beta.42`,
  PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector, and Node 24+. Do not replace the Workflow pin with `latest`,
  `beta`, a caret or a tilde: beta releases can change runtime compatibility.
- Start Postgres, then run `npm run db:bootstrap` before starting the agent. The generated
  script loads `.env.local`; invoking the upstream bootstrap CLI directly can use the wrong
  environment. The dashboard is a generated Compose profile, not a separate clone.
- Primary navigation: Today, Tasks, Routines, Connections, Knowledge. Settings and Diagnostics
  retain readiness, spend, notifications, traces, queue checks and execution inspection.
- The dashboard reads `workflow.workflow_runs.attributes` over SQL. OTLP trace capture is a
  separate source of prompt/tool detail, subject to capture and retention settings. Missing
  evidence and unpriced models must remain explicit. Estimated costs are not provider invoices.
- Routine dispatch uses durable claims, deduplicated manual requests, revision snapshots and
  overlap limits. Unknown dispatch pauses for investigation; automatic repeat is unsafe.
  The dashboard process and routine clock must remain up for scheduled work to dispatch.
- Approvals apply to configured gated tools. Prompt wording and skill frontmatter do not
  enforce permissions. Sandbox isolation depends on actual tools, backend, mounts and network.
- Cancellation is cooperative. A 202 acknowledgement does not prove termination. Inspect the
  task before replaying; successful tools may already have changed external systems.
- Shared credentials identify an installation, not a teammate. Do not claim team RBAC or
  tenant isolation. MCP control and approvals require separate explicit opt-ins.
- Saved budgets only enforce through opted-in hooks. Unobserved activation and unknown prices
  are visible. In-flight calls can incur charges. Notification retries can duplicate receipt.
- Memory review/correction proposals do not update embeddings. Real scoped memory tools must
  apply corrections. Skill reviews bind to content/source hashes and new per-file baselines;
  reviews are observations, not permission grants or proofs of safety.
- Preserve Postgres and private configuration through upgrades. Respect additive schema guards;
  never drop the evestack schema as repair advice. Inspect restored pending work before starting
  workers, because it can resume external actions. Use `/docs/backup-restore`.
- Read `RELEASE_PLAN.md` for exact-commit evidence. Local fixtures do not establish live provider
  success, repository access, external channel receipt or real-user adoption.
